sources.entry: PostHog - Product analytics, session recording, feature flagging and a/b testing that you can self-host (alternative to Mixpanel, Amplitude, Heap, HotJar, Optimizely). (Source Code) MIT Python

summary.one_liner: PostHog is an open-source product analytics platform that bundles web and product analytics, session replay, error tracking, feature flags, experiments, surveys, and data pipelines, and can be self-hosted or used as a cloud service.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes PostHog as a platform that ingests and stores product analytics, errors, session replays, logs, and business data for querying. Its listed capabilities include event-based product analytics (autocapture or manual instrumentation, with visualizations or SQL), a GA-like web analytics dashboard, group analytics, session replay with heatmaps, error tracking, logs, and tracing. It also covers feature flags, A/B experiments, early access features, no-code surveys, a support chat widget with inbox, and workflows triggered by product data. Data features include a managed warehouse with a SQL editor, data pipelines that send data to 25+ tools or webhooks, and custom API endpoints. The README also mentions AI observability for LLM apps and an MCP server for connecting agents. For self-hosting, it describes a one-line Docker-based hobby deploy on Linux.
use_cases: error tracking and logs for web apps
how_to_run: Cloud: sign up for PostHog Cloud US or EU
Self-host: run the one-line hobby deploy script on Linux with Docker (README recommends 4GB memory); the script URL is truncated in the README
Set up the app with the wizard: npx -y @posthog/wizard@latest
Or install a JavaScript snippet, one of the SDKs, or use the API
notable: Single platform covering analytics, session replay, feature flags, experiments, error tracking, and surveys
Hobby self-host deploy in one line with Docker
Setup wizard that installs PostHog into an app via npx
MCP server so AI agents can query product data
Managed warehouse with SQL editor and 120+ sources
caveats: Open-source self-hosted deployments are said to scale to about 100k events per month; the README recommends moving to PostHog Cloud beyond that
The README states no customer support or guarantees are provided for open-source deployments
Some features are marked beta (MCP analytics, early access features)
